chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Musa from Ahmad ibn Hamzah al-Qummi from Muhammad ibn Khallid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Zurarah from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a group of men who go out hunting together, where the dog belongs to one of them, the owner sends his dog, and another person names it (calls it by name); is that sufficient? He said: 'Only the owner who sent it may name it.'
ai.seo_question: Who is permitted to name the hunting dog during a group hunt in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the ritual validity of communal hunting by establishing that the act of invoking God's name (tasmiyah) is tied to the specific agency of the dog's owner who releases it. In Shia jurisprudence, this underscores the principle that the physical control and intent of the owner are prerequisites for the meat to be considered halal for others participating in the hunt. It highlights the precision required in transferring the ritual status of the catch through proper ownership and invocation.
